message.reasoning:
I need to build a NodeTest class that tests the abstract Node class through concrete jsoup implementations like TextNode and Element, since Node itself can't be instantiated directly. I'm also considering that this is Defects4J Jsoup-10b, so the jsoup source should already be present in the project rather than needing a separate jar.

I'm mapping out which Node methods to test through these subclasses - things like the constructor validation (baseUri and attributes can't be null), checking how Element and TextNode inherit and expose Node's behavior, and working out the right way to exercise the protected constructor indirectly through public subclass constructors.

Adding more test cases for attribute handling, baseUri trimming behavior, and abs: prefix lookups for missing attributes.

Also testing empty key validation throwing, plus absUrl cases: no href attribute returns empty string, relative href resolving against baseUri correctly, and an already-absolute href staying unchanged regardless of baseUri.

For malformed cases, I'm checking that a bad baseUri still resolves correctly if the href itself is absolute, but returns empty string when both baseUri and href are malformed, since the inner exception handling falls through to the outer catch block.

Since addChildren, reparentChild, removeChild, and similar methods are protected, I'll put the NodeTest class in the same org.jsoup.nodes package so it can access these package-protected methods directly for testing.

I'm reconsidering whether to actually declare a package statement at all—since putting the test in org.jsoup.nodes would avoid needing imports for Node, Element, TextNode, etc., but the instruction explicitly asks for imports, so I should keep the import statements even if technically redundant within the same package.

Importing a class from its own package isn't actually an error in Java, so I'll just include it as a comment for clarity per instructions. Since the tests live in the same package, I can access protected members directly, which means I can create a minimal concrete subclass of Node to test its constructors directly, exposing both the baseUri-and-attributes and baseUri-only constructors for validation testing.

This gives full control over testing without the complications Element, TextNode, or Document might introduce with their own extra logic, making it the cleanest way to unit test the abstract Node class. I'll build this as a static nested helper class within NodeTest.

Still writing test scaffolding...

Finishing TestNode constructors...

Now I'm planning constructor tests: verifying that a baseUri with surrounding whitespace gets trimmed, and that passing a null baseUri should throw since Validate.notNull is expected to raise an IllegalArgumentException.

Since I'm not fully certain about the exact exception type without seeing the Validate class source, I'll note that assumption with a comment in the test and proceed using IllegalArgumentException as the expected exception for both null baseUri and null attributes cases, then move on to the test checking construction with baseUri only.

For the default attributes test, I'll avoid depending on any unknown Attributes API beyond what Node itself exposes, just confirming attributes() isn't null and hasAttr returns false for an arbitrary key. For the no-arg constructor case, I'm noting that attributes() would be null and calling attr() could NPE since hasAttr relies on attributes.hasKey—this seems like a genuine edge case worth testing explicitly.

Then I'm planning a set of attribute-related tests: setting and getting attributes, getting a missing attribute (should return empty string), the "abs:" prefix case with no matching attribute, null-key validation on attr/hasAttr/removeAttr throwing exceptions, and removing an existing attribute.

Beyond that, I'm outlining tests for baseUri (setting it, and null throwing), followed by a batch for absUrl covering empty-key validation, missing attributes returning empty, relative URLs resolving against the base, already-absolute URLs passing through unchanged, and the malformed-base edge cases where a relative URL either falls back to its external form or resolves to empty.

I also want coverage for child node management: adding children, verifying childNodes is unmodifiable, accessing the protected array form, confirming parent starts null, reparenting removes from the old parent first, removal validates a non-null parent and actually detaches the node, replaceWith null-checks both the replacement and parent, child replacement works directly via the protected method, and removal correctly reindexes siblings, plus adding multiple children at once.

Then I'm planning sibling-related tests: iterating sibling nodes, next/previous sibling behavior at boundaries and for root nodes, adding children at a specific index with null-element validation, and reparenting via addChildren. I also want to flag an asymmetry bug where previousSibling() throws NPE on a parentless node while nextSibling() safely returns null -- worth a dedicated test to document that difference.

I'm also mapping out ownerDocument tests: confirming it returns null when there's no Document ancestor, and verifying it correctly resolves to a Document instance when one exists in the ancestry, plus checking that calling ownerDocument() directly on a Document returns itself.

For outerHtml/toString, I'm verifying the test node correctly wraps its head and tail output into "<test></test>", that outputSettings resolves properly through a default empty Document when there's no owner, and that toString() stays consistent with outerHtml(). I'm also confirming NodeTraversor calls both head and tail correctly since the node name isn't "#text", so the tail callback won't be skipped.

Now I'm planning nested-node traversal tests to confirm parent head, children, then parent tail ordering, plus equals/hashCode tests checking reference equality, consistent hashing, and that different objects are never equal even with identical content. I'm also outlining clone tests to ensure a cloned node becomes a parentless orphan copy.

Deep-copy clone tests should verify child nodes get distinct instances while still being linked to the cloned parent and preserving their original sibling indices, plus attribute cloning tests confirming Attributes.clone() produces a separate but equal copy.

For addChildren, I need to cover null-element validation via Validate.noNullElements, correct insertion order at a given index, and reparenting behavior where a child already attached elsewhere gets removed from its old parent's childNodes and reassigned proper sibling indices.

I should also test the protected replaceChild method directly: replacing an existing child with a new node and confirming parent/child references update correctly, that Validate.isTrue enforces the old node must actually belong to that parent, and that if the incoming node already has a different parent, it gets detached from that parent inline before being inserted.

I also want coverage for removeChild's parent-validation failure case, boundary checks on childNode(index), childNodesAsArray reflecting current state, and the edge case where siblingNodes() on a root node throws NullPointerException since parent() returns null.

With so many cases to cover, I'll write the tests comprehensively but keep them organized, grouping related assertions where it makes sense while still separating others for clarity. I'll also need a helper for building Attributes objects, relying on the put, get, hasKey, remove, and clone methods that Node already uses.

Writing test imports...

Now I'm drafting the nested TestNode class, checking that the abstract method signatures for outerHtmlHead, outerHtmlTail, and nodeName match exactly what's expected, and confirming I can get an OutputSettings instance via a default Document.

I'm assuming Attributes has a public no-arg constructor, and that Validate's methods (notNull, notEmpty, isTrue, noNullElements) throw IllegalArgumentException based on typical jsoup conventions -- I'll note this assumption in a comment in case it needs adjusting later.

Since childNodesAsArray() is package-protected, I can call it directly from the test in the same package. For ownerDocument tests, I'll trust that a compatible Document class with a baseUri constructor and outputSettings() method exists in the compiled classpath.

Rather than a shared setUp(), I'll construct TestNode instances inline per test since requirements vary. I also want to verify equals() behavior -- two separate instances with identical attributes should not be equal since the implementation likely relies on reference equality, while a node compared to itself should return true.

For hashCode, since it's computed recursively from parentNode and attributes, I won't assert an exact precomputed value -- instead I'll just check it's deterministic across repeated calls on the same object, and skip strict inequality checks between differently-configured nodes since that's not guaranteed. I also want to confirm attr(String,String) returns the same node instance for chaining, and that attributes() returns the exact same object reference that was passed into the constructor.

I should also test baseUri() with an empty string edge case -- since the constructor only validates notNull (not notEmpty), setting an empty baseUri should be allowed and should return "" afterward. Then I want to verify the attr() method's case-insensitive handling of the "abs:" prefix by testing with a mixed-case key like "ABS:href" to confirm it still triggers the absUrl branch.

I also want to cover the notEmpty validation on attributeKey by testing an empty string, which should throw, while being careful not to over-assume behavior for null inputs since that depends on implementation details. Beyond that, I should add a boundary test for childNode(index) covering both valid indices and an out-of-bounds case, then move on to writing the final test code with a nested TestNode class and clearly commented test groups mapping to each branch.

I also want to directly test setParentNode's reparenting quirk: calling it manually on a child moves the parent pointer and removes the child from its old parent's list via removeChild, but it doesn't actually insert the child into the new parent's childNodes list -- that only happens through higher-level methods like addChildren. This is a subtle existing behavior worth verifying explicitly.

Next I'll write a removeChild test that checks sibling index reindexing after removing a middle child from a three-child parent, confirming the remaining children shift to positions 0 and 1 and the removed child's parent becomes null. Then I'll test addChildren(int, ...) inserting a new child at a specific position among existing children, verifying correct ordering and reindexing, plus confirming that passing a null element in the array triggers a validation exception.

I'm also tracing through the addChildren logic for multiple new children: since it inserts in reverse order at the same index repeatedly, I verify that parent [c0,c1] calling addChildren(1, n1, n2) correctly produces [c0, n1, n2, c1] - matching the expected final ordering for the test case.

For the test file, I'll rely on existing NodeTraversor/NodeVisitor classes and only exercise Document's output settings indirectly through outerHtml() rather than instantiating them directly, trusting the empty-string Document constructor referenced in Node's own source. I also want to add boundary tests for childNode(-1) and childNode(size) throwing IndexOutOfBoundsException, plus confirming childNodes() returns an unmodifiable list that throws on add attempts.

I'm planning to organize the test methods into clear sections with descriptive names, using JUnit4's expected attribute for exception cases rather than try/catch blocks. Given length limits, I'm trimming my planned ~40 test methods down to roughly 35, covering constructor validation, default state checks, and core branch coverage.

Continuing the list now: attribute getter/setter chaining, missing key behavior, abs-prefix URL resolution, null key exceptions for attr/hasAttr/removeAttr, attribute removal and reference checks, then baseUri setting/getting including null and empty cases, moving into absUrl tests next.

Adding more test cases covering child-node insertion, reparenting, removal with sibling reindexing, and child replacement logic...

I'm continuing to list out test cases covering sibling index, owner document resolution, outer HTML rendering, equals/hashCode semantics, and cloning behavior.

That gives around 64 test methods total, which feels thorough but possibly excessive given the requirement for maximum branch coverage. I'll trim redundant cases where logical, aiming to settle around 55-60 methods while still covering everything comprehensively.

Writing test implementations now, making sure exception types like IllegalArgumentException from Validate checks are handled correctly, and verifying assumptions about the Attributes no-arg constructor and other minimal APIs match the actual jsoup source tree so the code compiles properly.

Writing outerHtml tests...

I then verify toString() matches outerHtml(), add basic equals/hashCode checks, and start writing clone tests that confirm a cloned child node becomes independent of its parent while keeping its own attributes intact.

For the deep-copy test, I set up a root with two children and clone the root, verifying that cloned children preserve their original sibling indices since their parent reference during cloning isn't null.

I should also check the default constructor case: it sets childNodes to an immutable empty list, so calling addChildren would throw UnsupportedOperationException. That's worth its own test to catch this extra branch. The indexOutOfBounds case for childNode(0) on an empty list is just the normal empty scenario though, so I don't need a separate test for that.

I'm also noting that the default constructor leaves baseUri unset, so baseUri() returns null—I should add an assertion checking that alongside the empty childNodes and null attributes test. For the abs: prefix test, I need a valid baseUri so absUrl logic actually reaches the hasAttr check when there's no href attribute at all.

I should also verify the case-insensitive abs: handling—like attr("ABS:href") resolving correctly against a relative href and baseUri—and confirm the substring logic strips "abs:" using a fixed length of 4 regardless of the original casing, since it operates on the original attributeKey string rather than the lowercased version.

Then I'll check relative URL resolution: a baseUri ending in a trailing slash combined with a relative href should join into a proper absolute URL, relying on standard URL resolution semantics.

For already-absolute hrefs, I'm verifying that if the href itself has a scheme, it overrides the base entirely, so the result matches parsing the href alone regardless of the base context.

For malformed base cases, I'm handling the fallback: if the base string isn't a valid URL on its own, catch the exception and try parsing the href directly as an absolute URL instead.

If both base and href fail to parse, the outer catch should just return an empty string.

Now I'm ready to finalize the full solution -- package declaration, imports, the test helper class, all test methods with assertions, plus a disclaimer comment about exception handling assumptions, followed by a summary table in Thai per the instructions.
